name: security-etcd-client-authority-review
intent: etcd client authentication and key-prefix authorization
artifacts: Client TLS identity, user/role mapping, prefix permissions, gateway paths and auth-enable state.
trace: Follow verified client identity into effective key-prefix operations and distinguish server transport trust from enabled application authorization.
experiment: Use an isolated etcd fixture with synthetic prefixes and two owned clients; compare rightful read/write and a restricted prefix operation.
disproof: TLS connection success is not key authorization, and endpoint metadata is not confidential key-value exposure.
repair: Bind client identities and prefix grants consistently across enabled interfaces and verify intended operations.
branch_decisions: Confirm authentication is enabled and which certificate or token maps to the effective user and roles. Prefix range permissions depend on the actual byte interval, not a human-readable prefix label. A TLS connection is not an authorization check; use tiny owned keys and inspect both point and range operations without dumping the keyspace.
